what_its_for: Procarbazine is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat Hodgkin's lymphoma (a type of cancer that affects the lymph nodes). It is usually given as part of a combination treatment plan with other cancer medicines.
how_to_take: Take procarbazine by mouth with a full glass of water. You can take it with food if it upsets your stomach. Take it exactly as your doctor tells you. Do not crush, chew, or break the capsules — swallow them whole. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your body weight, overall health, and how well the medicine is working. The typical dose is adjusted every few days, usually starting low and slowly increasing. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store procarbazine capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: AVOID alcohol completely while taking this medicine — drinking alcohol can cause a serious and dangerous reaction including severe headache, nausea, vomiting, flushing, fast heartbeat, and high blood pressure. AVOID foods high in tyramine such as aged cheeses, cured or smoked meats, fermented products, red wine, beer, sauerkraut, soy sauce, and overripe bananas, as this can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure. AVOID taking other medicines including over-the-counter drugs, cold medicines, decongestants, antidepressants, or herbal supplements without first asking your doctor or pharmacist. AVOID driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, drowsy, or confused. AVOID getting vaccinations (especially live vaccines) without your doctor's approval. AVOID contact with people who are sick, as your immune system may be weakened.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor RIGHT AWAY or go to the emergency room if you have: a sudden or severe headache, chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, signs of infection (fever over 100.4°F, chills, sore throat), unusual bleeding or bruising, blood in your urine or stool, severe nausea or vomiting that will not stop, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), seizures, confusion or difficulty thinking clearly, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, or swelling of the hands, feet, or ankles. Also call your doctor if you notice any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face or throat.
when_it_works: Procarbazine begins working inside your body right away, but you may not feel or see the effects immediately. It typically takes several weeks of treatment before your doctor can tell if the medicine is helping. Your doctor will check your blood counts and do tests regularly to see how you are responding to treatment. Be patient and attend all follow-up appointments.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Do not use procarbazine if you are pregnant. It can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Both men and women should use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after. Talk to your doctor before trying to get pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. CHILDREN: Use in children should be closely monitored by a specialist. OLDER ADULTS: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects and may need closer monitoring. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
